propositions: ~200 lines of production logic in YAML run-blocks (staleness classification, two alert-lifecycle state machines with find/open/comment/close steps) are untestable by linters and carry high defect density; migration to Python module with unit tests is needed.

Classification logic (api-error vs never-succeeded vs stale vs fresh) and four alert-lifecycle transition families (open-when-none, dedup-find, comment-when-stale, close-on-recovery) must move from YAML into scripts/canary_bridge.py with discrete subcommands and unit test coverage.
CAS push loops (reconcile-bridge.yml commit-back and canary flush) must remain in YAML byte-identical and pass existing verbatim-execution tests to avoid introducing an untested-glue drift seam.

Error handling dispositions from the original YAML must be preserved: alert-lifecycle writes fail loud (non-zero exit), dedup finds degrade gracefully to empty on CLI failure, and rebar bridge-fsck exit-code-1-with-valid-JSON must be interpreted as drift-detected not error.
DRY_RUN env var must gate all rebar mutations at the subcommand level (defense in depth against dropped if: conditions) and GITHUB_OUTPUT emission must match the original format exactly.
